note: Forbidden shapes, matched in this order. Shapes only, no vendor names; fixture hosts are example.invalid. A tool's tests grep their own output with `patterns`; `cases` prove the rewrite; `clean` is what must survive untouched. Decided on the first card: the path of a secrets file (~/.<tool>/.env) is not a secret and stays, because the spec's own error hint prints one; its contents never reach an envelope. The two token samples are deliberately mis-shaped for a vendor scanner while still matching the regexes above: the numeric one carries a 12-digit id and a secret part that starts with no known prefix, the three-segment one is 23.7.40 rather than any real length. A push protection rule blocks a public repository on a sample that looks live, so a sample that looks live costs the tools their commits - keep new samples shape-valid and vendor-invalid.

patterns.name: token_numeric_colon
patterns.about: a bot token shaped <8 or more digits>:<35 url-safe characters>; the digit run is open-ended because bot ids grow

patterns.name: token_three_segment
patterns.about: a bot token shaped <23-28>.<6-7>.<27+> url-safe characters

patterns.name: app_hash_hex32
patterns.about: a 32-character lowercase hex application hash; an md5 checksum or an undashed UUID has the same shape and is redacted too, the safe side

patterns.name: phone_plus
patterns.about: an international phone number written with a leading plus, 7 to 15 digits with optional separators; reduced to its last two digits. A signed count like +1234567 has the same shape and is reduced too; counts in a result are numbers, not strings, so this only bites prose

patterns.name: phone_double_zero
patterns.about: an international phone number written with a leading 00; reduced to its last two digits

patterns.name: session_path_profile
patterns.about: a session file path under profiles/<name>/, replaced by the profile it belongs to

patterns.name: session_path_legacy
patterns.about: any other session file path, which belongs to the default profile

patterns.name: webhook_url
patterns.about: a webhook URL whose path is /api/webhooks/<id>/<token>; the token segment is replaced

patterns.name: invite_link
patterns.about: a chat invite link with a /+<hash> or /joinchat/<hash> path; kept only when showing one is the command's purpose

clean: add 1542641014190375072 to the allowlist in ~/.x-tools/.env, or run without --yes
